## Triage complete - [x] Prepare the workspace: ready - [x] Install dependencies: complete - [x] Build the project: complete - [x] Reproduce the issue: confirmed - [x] Diagnose the cause: high confidence - [x] Verify the diagnosis: bug - [x] Attempt a fix: verified - [x] Publish the result: set `triage: fix pending` --- - **Reproduced:** Yes (build-output level — the `$0` token in generated config and the missing entrypoint validation are deterministic; the intermittent Vercel proxy substitution failure is host-specific but the code defect enabling it is confirmed) - **Exploration:** Yes — [View branch](https://github.com/withastro/astro/compare/factory/fix-18028?expand=1) - **Unit Test:** Yes — `packages/integrations/vercel/test/isr.test.ts` (two new tests: `'ignores x_astro_path that does not start with /'` and `'uses $1 (not $0) in ISR route dest'`) - **Priority:** **P4: important.** This affects all `@astrojs/vercel` ISR users without edge middleware. When the undocumented `$0` substitution fails, it causes multi-hour cache poisoning per CDN region, serving `301` redirects to nonsense URLs until the next deployment or ISR expiration. `getIsrPath` in `packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts` uses the undocumented `$0` capture reference in Vercel route `dest` fields. Vercel's own reference router excludes `0` from its substitution character class (`[1-9a-zA-Z]`), and when its production proxy intermittently fails to substitute `$0`, the entrypoint in `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts` silently accepts the literal `"$0"` string (it only checks `typeof realPath === 'string'`), resolves it to pathname `/$0`, and with `trailingSlash: 'always'` emits a cacheable `301` redirect to `/$0/`. The path token (`x_astro_path_token`) doesn't catch this because it's a literal in `dest` and always substitutes correctly. **I found a potential fix for this issue.** The fix applies both mitigations suggested in the issue: (a) replaces `$0` with `$1` by wrapping each ISR route's `src` regex in an outer capture group (e.g. `^/one/?$` → `^(/one/?)$`), bringing the substitution within Vercel's documented range; and (b) adds a `realPath.startsWith('/')` check in the entrypoint as defense in depth, so any future substitution failure results in a 404 instead of a cached redirect to a nonsense path. ### Try this fix You can test this fix right now without waiting for a release: ```sh # @astrojs/vercel npm i https://pkg.pr.new/@astrojs/vercel@440a893 ``` If this fixes your issue, please leave a comment letting us know (for example "confirmed, this fixes it"). A pull request will then be opened to get it merged.
Full Triage Report ## Issue Details **Title:** @astrojs/vercel: ISR routes can serve a cached redirect to /$0 when Vercel doesn't substitute the undocumented $0 token **Author:** @leifmarcus (CONTRIBUTOR) **Environment:** - Astro v7.3.2 - Node v24.18.0 - @astrojs/vercel v11.0.10 - `output: 'server'`, `trailingSlash: 'always'` - Vercel adapter with `isr: { expiration: , bypassToken: … }` ## Root Cause Two interrelated defects in the `@astrojs/vercel` ISR implementation: ### Defect 1: Reliance on undocumented `$0` token `getIsrPath` in `packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts` (line 75) generates `$0` in the `dest` of every ISR route: ```ts const getIsrPath = (pathToken: string) => `/_isr?${ASTRO_PATH_PARAM}=$0&${ASTRO_PATH_TOKEN_PARAM}=${pathToken}`; ``` Vercel's reference router uses `/\$([1-9a-zA-Z]+)/g` for substitution — `0` is excluded from the character class. The production proxy handles `$0` most of the time but has no documented guarantee, and failures have been observed. ### Defect 2: Missing path validation in entrypoint `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts` (line 32) only checks `typeof realPath === 'string'`. When `$0` isn't substituted, the literal `"$0"` passes this check, resolves to pathname `/$0` via `new URL("$0", url)`, and with `trailingSlash: 'always'` produces a `301` redirect to `/$0/` that gets cached for the ISR expiration window. ### Code Paths - **Without edge middleware** (affected): Routes use `dest = "/_isr?x_astro_path=$0&..."` directly. - **With edge middleware** (NOT affected): The middleware's `forwardPath` constructs the URL at runtime from `pathname`. ## Fix Applied 1. **`packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts`**: Changed `$0` → `$1` in `getIsrPath`. Added `wrapPatternInCaptureGroup()` to wrap each ISR route's `src` regex in an outer group (`^/one/?$` → `^(/one/?)$`). 2. **`packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts`**: Added `realPath.startsWith('/')` check. 3. **Tests**: Updated expected assertions in `test/isr.test.ts` and `test/isr-edge-middleware.test.ts`. Added two new regression tests. 4. **Changeset**: `.changeset/fix-isr-dollar-zero.md` for `@astrojs/vercel` patch. ### Verification - All 30 ISR, ISR-edge-middleware, and path-override-security tests pass. - Full Vercel adapter test suite (78 tests): 0 failures.
_This report was made by an LLM. The analysis may be wrong, and the potential fix might not work, but is intended as a starting point for exploring the issue._
Bot, I can confirm this fixes the issue.
The fix has been verified! A pull request has been created: https://github.com/withastro/astro/pull/18044

We added the fix and ran some tests on our preview environment. So far we could not find any issues, but can also not yet fully ensure, that the issue is fully resolved. At least, the pages are working correctly.

Today I received a support message from Vercel which confirms, that this change is fixing the issue:

> $0 is not part of the Build Output API contract. Only $1, $2 and named captures are supported. Any substitution of $0 you have seen is incidental behaviour and should not be relied on. The adapter change that switches to $1 and validates the path is the correct fix, and it has now merged upstream as [withastro/astro#18044](https://github.com/withastro/astro/issues/18044) with a patch release of @astrojs/vercel to follow.
